plan: This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: I pay the second-highest bid if I win, since the clock stops at the second-highest exit price. In such mechanisms, bidding my true value is optimal (a dominant strategy), as it ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the price I'd pay, and avoids overpaying or losing profitable opportunities. My value is $6, so I will bid exactly $6.

This auction mechanism functions like a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, regardless of their own bid (as long as they have the highest bid). This makes truthful bidding a dominant strategy - bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids (positive profit) and lose when it's lower (avoiding losses). Bidding above value risks winning at a price exceeding my value; bidding below risks losing profitable auctions. Therefore, I will bid my true value of $40.

Since this is effectively a second-price sealed-bid auction (winner pays the second-highest bid), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding exactly $28 ensures I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids and pay only the second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit without risk of overpaying or losing profitable opportunities.
